figures.finding: Taking part in a performance, display, activity, contest or event for advertising, beauty, sport, educational, religious, traditional, cultural or artistic purposes isn't employment under the Labour Act's child-labour section: if it earns no income (or only for a charity, school or religious body) no licence is needed; if it generates income for anyone, a licence must first be obtained from a children's commissioner and its regulations and conditions met, with a parent's, guardian's or care-giver's written consent; activities authorised by a local or regional council are outside the licence rule, and the Minister may prohibit some by regulation. No child may be induced or allowed into any labour or performance that is harmful, inappropriate for his age or risks his well-being or education, or forced into a performance save school or reasonable parental authority. The exemption covers participating in the performance; a child writing or directing as employment falls under the Labour Act's general bar under fourteen (reading).

value.permit: licence from a children's commissioner (income-generating participation)
value.consent: parent's, guardian's or care-giver's written consent

figures.applies: Child Care and Protection Act, 2015 (Act No. 3 of 2015), s. 234.

figures.finding: The Namibia Film Commission's fund backs established and emerging filmmakers expected to be Namibian residents committed to a career in film and television (an experienced filmmaker needs at least two screen credits); full-time employees of networks or training institutions can't apply; no applicant age is set.

value.applicant: Namibian residents; preference for Namibian writers, directors, producers
value.excluded: full-time staff of TV networks or training institutions

sources.said: Preference will be given to projects that involve Namibian writers, directors, and/or producers. ... The NFC encourages the work of established and emerging filmmakers who are committed to a serious career in the film and television industry. Applicants are expected to be Namibian residents ... Full-time practitioners employed by television networks or training institutions are not eligible to apply.
